season: none: all year (the layer has no season and the City names none)

holidays.note: The City: "Street sweeping will not occur on the following City of Oakland holidays." The tickets agree, night sweeps included (holidayCheck).

lineSides.note: Each line's odd and even side (a major street drawn as two lines counts its one side): why it has rules or not, from the City's codes.

notPosted.why: code N-S, "No Signage": swept, but no signs, so not enforced

noHours.why: a day code with time NA

sideUnknown.why: two different schedules and no way to tell which side holds the odd numbers

contradicted.why: the tickets contradict the schedule (crossCheck.contradictedSides): left off the map, --keep-contradicted keeps them

sidePlacement.note: byNumbers: the address ranges say which side is odd (checked against the City's address points, which win where they clearly disagree); byAddressPoints: no ranges, the address points say; byNeighbors: the next line of the same street does; bothSidesSame: unknown, but both sides share one schedule; major streets (MS, two lines, one side each): the curb is on the side of the line's house numbers, else the side away from the street's other line. The tickets' own points were not used: they sit on the side the address points give on only about 80% of blocks.

repeatedNames.note: The layer repeats a line once per name; when its copies give a side different schedules, the tickets on that side choose, else the primary record.

snapshot2024.note: Every 2024 line is a 2021 line (same geometry). Its schedule equals the 2021 primary record's, or another copy of the same line in the 2021 layer; it holds no schedule the 2021 layer lacks, so it changes nothing by itself. Where it differs, the tickets chose (repeatedNames).

weeksCheck.1st and 3rd: 99.9% of 73153 tickets on that weekday and hours fall in those weeks

weeksCheck.every week: 100% of 98028 tickets on that weekday and hours fall in those weeks

crossCheck.method: Each ticket goes to the line of its written street whose house numbers hold its number (on a major street, the line that carries that side), nearest the ticket's point; its side is odd or even by the number. It agrees when the side has a rule for that weekday, that week of the month and that hour (10 minute grace at both ends of the window).
crossCheck.reading: Daytime residential routes agree (most 80 to 92%). The night routes on main streets (10 to 14) and the weekend routes (W2 to W6) do not: blocks with odd and even reversed, other hours, and weekend sweeps that tickets now show on Thursday and Friday. About 6% of tickets land on sides the layer marks as not swept, mostly downtown and night streets.

swapped.rule: odd numbered tickets in the even side's windows AND even numbered tickets in the odd side's (each at least 3, three times those in their own window, and 40% of that side's tickets); a major street's two lines together
